question.problem:
The covariance matrix $C$ of some particular observations is shown below. 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the first principal component of the data, given that the eigenvalues of $C$ are $4$ and $2.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the unit eigenvectors of the covariance matrix $C$ are called the principal components of the data. If 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}>{\lambda }_{2}>⋯>{\lambda }_{n}
$$

are the eigenvalues of $C$ written in descending order, then: 

- the $1$st principal component is the unit eigenvector ${u}_{1}$ corresponding to the $1$st eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1},$

- the $2$nd principal component is the unit eigenvector ${u}_{2}$ corresponding to the $2$nd eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2},$

- $⋯$

and so on.

In our case, the eigenvalues of the covariance matrix $C,$ in descending order, are ${\lambda }_{1}=4$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2.$
So, we need the unit eigenvector that corresponds to the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}C-4I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]-4[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(C-4I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ 

Finally, dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{2},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
